plain_english: A young speech teacher came to see Epictetus. His hair was perfectly styled and his clothes were fancy. Epictetus said, "Tell me — don't you think some dogs are beautiful and some horses are beautiful? Same with all other animals?" The young man said, "Yes, I do." "Well then, aren't some people beautiful and others ugly?" "Definitely." "But do we call them beautiful for the same reasons, or does each thing have its own kind of beauty?" Epictetus continued: "Think about it this way. Dogs are naturally made for one purpose, horses for another, and nightingales for yet another. We can say each one is beautiful when it's excellent according to its own nature. But since each has a different nature, each is beautiful in a different way. Don't you think?" The young man agreed.
original_excerpt: A certain young man, a rhetorician, came to see Epictetus, with his hair dressed more carefully than was usual and his attire in an ornamental style; whereupon Epictetus said, Tell me if you do not think that some dogs are beautiful and some horses, and so of all other animals. I do think so, the youth replied. Are not then some men also beautiful and others ugly? Certainly. Do we then for the same reason call each of them in the same kind beautiful, or each beautiful for something peculiar? And you will judge of this matter thus. Since we see a dog naturally formed for one thing, and a horse for another, and for another still, as an example, a nightingale, we may generally and not improperly declare each of them to be beautiful then when it is most excellent according to its nature; but since the nature of each is different, each of them seems to me to be beautiful in a different way. Is it not so? He admitted that it was.

plain_english: What makes a dog beautiful makes a horse ugly. What makes a horse beautiful makes a dog ugly. This happens because they have different natures. Think about it this way: What makes a fighter good at pankration makes a wrestler weak and a runner look ridiculous. Someone who's built perfectly for the pentathlon looks terrible as a wrestler. "True," he said. So what makes a human beautiful? The same thing that makes a dog or horse beautiful in their own way. "Yes," he said. What makes a dog beautiful? Having the qualities that make a dog excellent. What makes a horse beautiful? Having the qualities that make a horse excellent.
original_excerpt: That then which makes a dog beautiful, makes a horse ugly; and that which makes a horse beautiful, makes a dog ugly, if it is true that their natures are different. It seems to be so. For I think that what makes a Pancratiast beautiful, makes a wrestler to be not good, and a runner to be most ridiculous; and he who is beautiful for the Pentathlon, is very ugly for wrestling. It is so, said he. What then makes a man beautiful? Is it that which in its kind makes both a dog and a horse beautiful? It is, he said. What then makes a dog beautiful? The possession of the excellence of a dog. And what makes a horse beautiful? The possession of the excellence of a horse.

plain_english: What makes a man beautiful? Having the excellence that makes someone truly human. So if you want to be beautiful, young man, work on this — getting human excellence. But what is that? Look at who you praise when you judge people fairly. Do you praise the just person or the unjust? The just. Do you praise the moderate person or the immoderate? The moderate. The self-controlled or the uncontrolled? The self-controlled. If you make yourself that kind of person, you'll know you've made yourself beautiful. But as long as you ignore these things, you'll be ugly — no matter how hard you try to appear beautiful.
original_excerpt: What then makes a man beautiful? Is it not the possession of the excellence of a man? And do you then, if you wish to be beautiful, young man, labor at this, the acquisition of human excellence? But what is this? Observe whom you yourself praise, when you praise many persons without partiality: do you praise the just or the unjust? The just. Whether do you praise the moderate or the immoderate? The moderate. And the temperate or the intemperate? The temperate. If then you make yourself such a person, you will know that you will make yourself beautiful; but so long as you neglect these things, you must be ugly, even though you contrive all you can to appear beautiful.
